question: Should `openclawProgressKind: "tool-progress"` become a supported public Plugin SDK contract, and must it preserve Slack’s configured standalone-progress delivery mode?
rationale: The branch adds third-party SDK surface and chooses transport semantics that currently conflict with documented Slack behavior, so implementation alone cannot establish the permanent API and compatibility policy.

options.title: Document and preserve configuration
options.body: Keep the narrow generic SDK intent, document its producer and transport semantics, and make Slack suppression conditional so configured standalone progress remains deliverable.

options.title: Internalize the intent
options.body: Remove the new public exports and route Codex-to-Slack progress through an existing internal or plugin-owned progress seam.

options.title: Accept unconditional suppression
options.body: Treat typed tool progress as never independently deliverable and explicitly revise Slack documentation and compatibility expectations before merge.

recommendation.title: Document and preserve configuration
recommendation.body: Keep the narrow generic SDK intent, document its producer and transport semantics, and make Slack suppression conditional so configured standalone progress remains deliverable.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history spans the affected Slack delivery state and Codex runtime boundaries, making this the strongest available routing candidate for the cross-boundary API decision.
